Q: Permission artifactregistry.repositories.uploadArtifacts denied on resource using github actions A:

I faced the same issue today. As per Artifacts registry page, below command needs to be run after gcloud login. Then push worked.

gcloud auth configure-docker gcr.io

Q: Convert MIDI file to list of notes with length and starting time A:

You can use any open-source library for parsing MIDI file and convert its data to text file in your desired format. For example, with the DryWetMIDI you can use this code:

public static void ConvertMidiToText(string midiFilePath, string textFilePath)
{
    var midiFile = MidiFile.Read(midiFilePath);

    File.WriteAllLines(
        textFilePath,
        midiFile
            .GetNotes()
            .Select(n => $"{n.NoteNumber} {n.Time} {n.Length}"));
}

ConvertMidiToText method will produce text files like this:

37 0 480
37 960 480
37 1920 480
37 2400 480
70 2640 192

where first number is note number (60 = C4), second one is starting time in MIDI ticks and the third one is length in MIDI ticks.

You can even write time and length in hours:minutes:seconds format. This code

public static void ConvertMidiToText(string midiFilePath, string textFilePath)
{
    var midiFile = MidiFile.Read(midiFilePath);
    TempoMap tempoMap = midiFile.GetTempoMap();

    File.WriteAllLines(
        textFilePath,
        midiFile
            .GetNotes()
            .Select(n => $"{n.NoteNumber} {n.TimeAs<MetricTimeSpan>(tempoMap)} {n.LengthAs<MetricTimeSpan>(tempoMap)}"));
}

will produce text like this:

37 00:00:00 00:00:00.4800000
37 00:00:00.9600000 00:00:00.4800000
37 00:00:01.9200000 00:00:00.4800000
37 00:00:02.4000000 00:00:00.4800000
70 00:00:02.6400000 00:00:00.1920000

More info on different time/length formats in the Time and length article.

Q: How can I fix "/usr/bin/ld: warning: trap.o: missing .note.GNU-stack section implies executable stack"? A:

IF (a big if, only relevant for some who get this message) the message appears due to a GCC compiler generating trampolines to implement nested functions, the warning can by removed by

-ftrampoline-impl=heap

This option moves trampoline from the stack to the heap and is used, for example, by https://github.com/conda-forge/ctng-compiler-activation-feedstock/issues/143

If the -z noexecstack flag is attempted on a code that places trampolines on the stack without moving them to the heap, the code will just crash. That flag really just silences the warning but does not fix the cause.

Q: DuckDB AWS Credential refresh A:

There is https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/core_extensions/aws#auto-refresh

CREATE SECRET env_test (
    TYPE s3,
    PROVIDER credential_chain,
    REFRESH auto
);

But also https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb-aws/issues/97

Q: how to match ssh config based on directory path A:

For future reader's, @iBug has the correct idea. Their answer put me on journey of discovery.

Building on what they said, here are a few Match ... exec commands I found to work quite well

git config user.email

# GitHub: Personal account
Match host github.com exec "[ $(git config user.email) == user.name@example-home.com ]"
  IdentityFile ...

# GitHub: Work account
Match host github.com exec "[ $(git config user.email) == user.name@example-work.com ]"
  IdentityFile ...

Pattern matching without grep

Note the * at the end of the path, this uses Bash built-in pattern matching

$PWD

Match host github.com exec "[[ $PWD == /home/username/work/* ]]"

git config

Match host github.com exec "[[ $(git config remote.origin.url) == git@github.com:pvt* ]]"

More

I didn't go further but I guess one can expand on all that [[ ]] offers, e.g.

  • regular expression matching (=~)
  • ability to use && and ||
